title: S1c worker_registry: durable runtime registry of running workers with structured events, reconciliation and read-only inspection CLI (P11, P12)
spec:
Create orchestrator/worker_registry.py. STATUSES = ("starting","running","waiting","steering","cancelling","cancelled","done","failed","held"). Files: .orchestrator/workers/<task>.json (one document: task, role, model, provider, account, pid, worktree, branch, started_at, last_event_at, stage, current_tool (only if the event stream reports it), tokens (input_uncached, cache_read, output so far when known), usd, elapsed_s (computed on read), parent, children (task ids created with constraints.fix_round_for or parent equal to this task while it runs), status, status_reason) and .orchestrator/workers/<task>.events.jsonl (append-only: ts, kind, data; kinds at least spawned, claimed, stage, tool, usage, exit, reconciled, held). Writes are atomic (temp file + rename) under the existing bus lock helper if one is exposed, else a registry-local fcntl lock. API: upsert(task_id, **fields), get(task_id), active(), event(task_id, kind, **data), finish(task_id, status, reason=None), reconcile(alive_fn=daemon.alive) marks entries whose pid is dead and status is running/starting as failed with reason process_dead and emits a reconciled event (no bus changes; daemon.reconcile_dead stays the authority for task status).
Wire producers with minimal edits: spawn.py where the claude -p Popen is created (around line 1046: spawned with pid, account, model, worktree, branch) and where the json result is parsed (around line 1084-1090: usage event + finish done/failed); executor.py where a codex exec thread starts and ends (provider codex, thread id as pid substitute in field thread, plus usage and finish); daemon.reconcile_dead calls worker_registry.reconcile at the end of its handling. Never store packet text, prompts, transcripts or secrets in the registry; only identifiers, numbers and event kinds. Never expose hidden reasoning: only observable runtime events.
CLI: `orchestrator workers [--task T-dddd] [--all] [--json]`: table of active workers (task, role, model, provider, status, stage, elapsed, tokens, worktree) and with --task the full document plus the last 20 events; --all includes finished ones from the last 24 h. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/03-worker-registry.md (document shape, event kinds, what is deliberately not recorded).
Spec review T-1000 folded in: (1) executor.py runs codex through one blocking subprocess.run (near line 159) and learns thread_id only after stdout is parsed: upsert the registry entry BEFORE launching (status starting, provider codex, model, worktree, branch, task, account codex) and replace subprocess.run with Popen plus communicate(timeout=...) preserving the existing timeout, capture and error semantics, so the pid is recorded at launch (event spawned with pid) and the entry is live for the whole run; add the thread id to the entry after parsing (event claimed or thread). Acceptance test: a patched Popen for codex shows an active entry with pid before communicate returns. (2) worker_registry.py never imports daemon (daemon imports it): reconcile(alive_fn) takes the function as a required argument, and daemon.tick calls worker_registry.reconcile(alive) exactly once per tick after the dead-task loop (not inside reconcile_dead). (3) children = task ids whose constraints.fix_round_for equals this task only (the parent field carries the goal container, never the spawning worker); drop the parent-based half of the definition; document that in 03-worker-registry.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. Read docs/context-economy/00-overview.md only if you need the evidence/decision_log conventions.

spec_review_risks.issue: Base spec text says reconcile(alive_fn=daemon.alive) and 'daemon.reconcile_dead calls worker_registry.reconcile at the end of its handling', but fold-in item (2) explicitly overrides this: alive_fn must be a required arg (a default of daemon.alive would force worker_registry to import daemon, which already imports worker_registry -> circular import) and the call site moves to daemon.tick (once per tick after the dead-task loop), not inside reconcile_dead (which runs once per dead task in a loop). The contradictory base wording was never struck, so an implementer reading top-to-bottom could wire the circular-import version.

Base 'Files:' section defines children as tasks with constraints.fix_round_for OR parent equal to this task. Verified against daemon.py: 'parent' on a task document is the goal container id (used throughout daemon.py for goal_id/base-branch resolution), never the spawning worker's id. Matching children by parent would make sibling tasks under the same goal falsely list each other as children. Fold-in item (3) correctly retracts the parent-based half but the base text still contains it, so the two definitions in the same packet conflict.

Fold-in item (1) requires replacing `r = subprocess.run(cmd, **run_kwargs)` (line 159) with Popen + communicate(timeout=...), 'preserving the existing timeout ... semantics'. That's not automatic: subprocess.run kills the child process internally before re-raising TimeoutExpired, but Popen.communicate does not. The existing `except subprocess.TimeoutExpired` handler (lines 160-161) just returns a failed result without killing the process -- it never needed to, because subprocess.run already killed it. A naive Popen swap will leak an orphaned `codex exec` process on every timeout unless the handler adds p.kill() (mirroring spawn.py's own TimeoutExpired handler at spawn.py:1049-1051). The spec should say this explicitly instead of implying 'preserve semantics' covers it for free.

Worse, at least six existing tests in this file (the fake_codex helper used across many tests, plus inline patches around lines 207-214, 227-233, 280-284) monkeypatch executor.subprocess.run directly to intercept the codex call; once _run() calls subprocess.Popen instead, those monkeypatches stop being hit, Popen tries to exec a real 'codex' binary (or raises FileNotFoundError, which _run does not catch), and every one of those pre-existing tests breaks. Because the file is out of scope, the executor also cannot fix those broken tests, so tests-green.sh cannot pass.

The spec's fold-in point (1) is otherwise correct and matches the code (subprocess.run at line 159 inside _run, single blocking call, thread_id only known after parsing stdout at line 168-169). No other issue with this part once scope is fixed.
